data_elements.name: Tool version
data_elements.description: Version or build of the referenced tool at execution time.

data_elements.name: Configuration profile
data_elements.description: Configuration, profile or parameter set in force at execution.

data_elements.name: Input snapshot reference
data_elements.description: Reference and digest of the input data snapshot used.

artifacts.name: Execution parameter manifest
artifacts.description: An immutable capture of the tool references, versions, configuration and input snapshot digests that the assessment relies on. It documents parameters; it does not schedule, invoke or control any evaluator, which remains owned by the referenced execution model.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Series key is the assessment identifier; a zero-padded monotonically increasing run sequence distinguishes manifests, with a cryptographic digest recorded at registration. The sequence is never derived from a date.

layers.name: Scale and Decision Rule
layers.description: The vocabulary and scale in which results are expressed, and the rule that converts them into a decision.

findings.name: Outcome scale and result vocabulary
findings.description: The measurement level, bounds and favourable direction of any numeric scale, the controlled vocabulary for non-numeric outcomes, and how indeterminate, inapplicable, untested and error states are kept distinct from a negative result.

questions.text: Is the outcome nominal, ordinal, interval or ratio, and what are its bounds?
Which controlled vocabulary expresses non-numeric outcomes for this assessment?
answer_data: Default value where no result is produced

questions.text: Which direction of the scale is favourable, and what are the best and worst attainable values?
How are untested, not-checked, error and not-selected states distinguished from a negative result?
answer_data: Rule forbidding coercion to a negative result
Downstream handling of each indeterminate value

data_elements.name: Scale definition reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the versioned scale definition in effect.

data_elements.name: Worst attainable value
data_elements.description: Lowest value the scale permits.

data_elements.name: Best attainable value
data_elements.description: Highest value the scale permits.

data_elements.name: Outcome code system
data_elements.description: Identifier and version of the vocabulary supplying outcome values.

findings.inline_only_rationale: A scale is definitional reference data — bounds, polarity, level of measurement and an enumerated vocabulary — that must be resolvable inline for any consumer to interpret a score. The authoritative scale and code-system documents are held by the vocabulary registry this model aligns to, so producing a local artifact would fork a governed vocabulary.

findings.name: Decision rule, thresholds and uncertainty handling
findings.description: The rule that converts scored or determined values into a conformity or grade decision, the cut scores, acceptance limits and guard bands it uses, how uncertainty is accounted for beforehand, and the conditions under which the assessment must abstain.

questions.text: What decision rule converts measured or scored values into a conformity or grade decision?
What cut scores, acceptance limits or guard bands apply, and who set them?
answer_data: Cut score or acceptance limit values

questions.text: How is measurement or rater uncertainty accounted for before the decision is taken?
answer_data: Risk of false accept or false reject accepted
Whether the rule is binary or non-binary

questions.text: Under what conditions must the assessment abstain rather than decide?
answer_data: How abstention is expressed in the outcome vocabulary

data_elements.name: Decision rule reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the versioned decision rule applied.

data_elements.name: Cut score or acceptance limit
data_elements.description: Threshold value separating outcome categories.

data_elements.name: Guard band
data_elements.description: Interval applied to acceptance limits to control decision risk.

data_elements.name: Abstention condition
data_elements.description: Condition requiring an indeterminate rather than a decided outcome.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The decision rule must be machine-readable inline so a consumer can re-derive the conclusion from the recorded values. Where the rule is published by a scheme or laboratory quality system, it is referenced by identifier and version; enforcing or executing the rule against live systems belongs to the referenced enforcement model, not here.

bundles.name: Evidence and Observation
bundles.description: What was relied on, how it links to criteria, whether it is sound, and what was actually observed.
bundles.rationale: OSCAL separates observations carrying evidence from findings that judge criteria; SP 800-53A ties evidence to determination statements; EARL requires a subject and a test behind every result. Evidence handling is therefore a distinct top-level concern from determination, and its quality qualifiers decide whether a conclusion is defensible.

layers.name: Evidence Corpus
layers.description: The evidence items relied on, their linkage to criteria, and their quality and admissibility.

findings.name: Evidence items and criterion linkage
findings.description: The discrete evidence items relied on, their types, the criterion or determination statement each supports or contradicts, and the times at which each was created, collected and received.

questions.text: What discrete evidence items were relied on, and of what type is each?
answer_data: Origin of each item (subject-supplied, assessor-collected, machine-generated)

questions.text: Which criterion or determination statement does each evidence item support or contradict?
answer_data: Weight or role of the item in the determination

questions.text: What makes the evidence set sufficient to support the determination for each criterion?
answer_data: Sufficiency rule or minimum evidence requirement
Gap statement where evidence is thin

questions.text: When was each evidence item created, collected and received?
answer_data: Receipt or ingestion time into the assessment

data_elements.name: Evidence item reference

data_elements.name: Evidence type
data_elements.description: Coded type of an evidence item.

data_elements.name: Evidence-criterion linkage
data_elements.description: Association between an evidence item and the criterion it bears on.

data_elements.name: Evidence collection time
data_elements.description: Time an evidence item was collected, distinct from when it was created.

artifacts.name: Evidence object
artifacts.description: A discrete item of evidence relied on by the assessment. The bytes and custody remain with the referenced evidence repository; the assessment registers the pointer, type and integrity digest.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Custody-system identifier issued by the referenced evidence repository takes priority; where none exists, a digest-derived content identifier plus a Dimension-assigned UUID. Filenames and collection dates are never identifiers.

artifacts.name: Evidence-to-criterion linkage register
artifacts.description: The register mapping each registered evidence item to the criteria and determinations it supports or contradicts, with sufficiency notes.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Series key is the assessment identifier; the sequence number is the assessment version the index belongs to, so each finalised version retains its own frozen index.

findings.name: Evidence quality, admissibility and reuse limits
findings.description: Whether each item is authentic and unaltered since collection, whether it is still current for the assessed state, which offered evidence was rejected or down-weighted, and which items carry confidentiality or personal-data constraints limiting reuse.

questions.text: How is each evidence item shown to be authentic and unaltered since collection?
answer_data: Custody assurance statement from the referenced repository

questions.text: Is the evidence still current for the assessed state, and when does it cease to be?
answer_data: Maximum permitted age per evidence type
Effect of staleness on dependent determinations

questions.text: Which offered evidence was rejected or down-weighted, and why?
Which evidence carries confidentiality, personal-data or privilege constraints that limit reuse?

data_elements.name: Evidence integrity digest
data_elements.description: Digest and algorithm recorded for an evidence item at registration.

data_elements.name: Evidence expiry
data_elements.description: Date after which an evidence item is no longer treated as current.

data_elements.name: Evidence exclusion reason
data_elements.description: Reason an offered evidence item was rejected or down-weighted.

data_elements.name: Evidence sensitivity class
data_elements.description: Confidentiality or personal-data classification of an evidence item.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Quality qualifiers are assertions attached to evidence already registered by the linkage finding: digests, expiry dates, exclusion reasons and sensitivity codes. The evidence bytes are held by the referenced custody model and the artifact for them is declared once, so restating them here would create a second registration of the same object.

layers.name: Observation and Measurement
layers.description: Raw observed results with distinct event and recording times, and the uncertainty and traceability that qualify quantitative values.

findings.name: Observation records, actors and timing
findings.description: The raw result observed or returned for each check before judgement is applied, the actor or device that produced it, the separation of the time the observed condition held from the time the observation was recorded, and the place of observation where it matters.

questions.text: What raw result was observed or returned for each check before judgement was applied?
answer_data: Raw observed value or return code
Reference to the check or item that produced it

questions.text: Which actor or device produced the observation, and under which role?
answer_data: Role in which the observer acted
Delegation chain where the observer acted on behalf of another

questions.text: How are the time the observed condition held and the time the observation was recorded kept distinct?
answer_data: Event time of the observed condition

questions.text: Where was the observation taken when site or environment materially affects the result?

data_elements.name: Observed value

data_elements.name: Observation method

data_elements.name: Observation event time
data_elements.description: Time at which the observed condition held.

data_elements.name: Observation recording time
data_elements.description: Time at which the observation was recorded or ingested.

artifacts.name: Raw result output
artifacts.description: The unmodified output of a check, field observation or candidate response session, retained so determinations can be re-derived from what was actually seen.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Series key is the assessment identifier combined with the producing tool or observer reference; sequence increments per run. Event time and recording time are carried inside the output, never used as its identifier.

findings.name: Measurement uncertainty and traceability
findings.description: The stated uncertainty of each quantitative result and how it was evaluated, the quantity, unit and reference scale each value belongs to, and the calibration or reference standard the measurement is traceable to.

questions.text: What is the stated uncertainty of each quantitative result and how was it evaluated?
answer_data: Evaluation method (Type A, Type B, replicate, expert)
Components contributing to the uncertainty budget

questions.text: Which quantity, unit and reference scale does each numeric value belong to?
To what reference standard or calibration is the measurement traceable?

data_elements.name: Measured quantity
data_elements.description: Quantitative result with its unit.

data_elements.name: Measurement uncertainty
data_elements.description: Stated uncertainty associated with a quantitative result.

data_elements.name: Unit code
data_elements.description: Unit of measure with its code system.

data_elements.name: Calibration reference
data_elements.description: Pointer to the calibration or reference standard establishing traceability.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Uncertainty statements, units and traceability pointers are declared values carried alongside each quantitative result. Calibration certificates and the traceability chain are produced and maintained by the referenced metrology model; this model neither runs calibration programmes nor issues those certificates, so it declares no artifact for them.

bundles.name: Determination, Scoring and Conclusion
bundles.description: Criterion-level verdicts and scores, their aggregation into a composite result, and the stated conclusion with its validity.
bundles.rationale: ISO/IEC 17000 distinguishes determination from review and from decision; OSCAL distinguishes observations from findings; XCCDF distinguishes rule-results from a scored TestResult. This bundle keeps criterion-level determination, aggregation and the accountable conclusion as separate, traceable steps rather than collapsing them into a single verdict.

layers.name: Criterion-Level Outcomes
layers.description: Per-criterion verdicts with rationale and locators, and the raw and normalised scores that accompany them.

findings.name: Criterion verdict, rationale and locator
findings.description: The outcome value assigned to each criterion from the bound vocabulary, the reasoning connecting cited evidence to that outcome, the severity or materiality of negative outcomes, and where in the subject each negative outcome occurs.

questions.text: What outcome value was assigned to each criterion, from which vocabulary?
answer_data: Whether the value is determined, indeterminate or not applicable

questions.text: What reasoning connects the cited evidence to each criterion outcome?
answer_data: References to the evidence items relied on
Assumptions made in reaching the outcome

questions.text: How are negative outcomes graded by severity or materiality?
answer_data: Threshold at which a negative outcome blocks a positive conclusion

questions.text: Where in the subject does each negative outcome occur?
answer_data: Pointer or locator into the subject

data_elements.name: Criterion outcome
data_elements.description: Outcome value assigned to a single criterion.

data_elements.name: Outcome rationale

data_elements.name: Nonconformity severity
data_elements.description: Graded severity or materiality of a negative outcome.

data_elements.name: Outcome locator
data_elements.description: Pointer identifying where in the subject a negative outcome occurs.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Criterion outcomes are structured values keyed to criterion identifiers and must be queryable, sortable and diffable as data rather than read out of a rendered document. The report that presents them to a reader is declared once by the conclusion finding, which keeps a single authoritative rendition.

findings.name: Criterion scores and normalisation
findings.description: The raw score recorded for each criterion against its maximum, how raw scores are normalised or rescaled before aggregation, and which scale definition version each recorded score refers to.

questions.text: What raw score, if any, was recorded for each criterion and against which maximum?
answer_data: Maximum attainable score for that criterion

questions.text: How are raw scores normalised or rescaled before aggregation?
Which scale definition version does each recorded score refer to?
answer_data: Scale reference with version per score
Rule when scale versions differ across criteria
Statement of whether historical scores are recomputed

data_elements.name: Raw score

data_elements.name: Maximum score
data_elements.description: Maximum attainable score for a criterion.

data_elements.name: Normalised score
data_elements.description: Score after normalisation or rescaling.

data_elements.name: Score scale reference
data_elements.description: Versioned scale definition a score is expressed against.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Scores are numeric data bound to a scale reference and must be recomputable and comparable across records. QTI keeps outcome variables as declared data separate from results reporting, and this finding follows that separation; the rendered scorecard is declared by the aggregation finding.

layers.name: Composite Result, Conclusion and Validity
layers.description: How criterion results roll up, what conclusion is stated and by whom, and for how long and under what conditions it holds.

findings.name: Aggregation model and composite result
findings.description: The scoring or aggregation model that combines criterion results, the weights and precedence rules it applies, the form in which the composite is expressed, and how it is computed when some criteria are untested or indeterminate.

questions.text: Which scoring or aggregation model combines criterion results into a composite result?
answer_data: Whether the model is documented as required for aggregated scores

questions.text: What weights or precedence rules apply, and how are unweighted and inapplicable items handled?
answer_data: Treatment of not-applicable and unweighted items

questions.text: How is the composite result expressed, and must its inputs be published alongside it?
answer_data: Composite form (score, level, grade, class, vector)
Vector or input string required for republication
Qualitative band mapping where one applies

questions.text: How is a composite computed when some criteria are untested or indeterminate?
answer_data: Rule for excluding or imputing missing results
Minimum completeness required for a composite
Flag marking a composite as partial

data_elements.name: Aggregation model

data_elements.name: Criterion weight

data_elements.name: Composite score
data_elements.description: Numeric composite produced by the aggregation model.

data_elements.name: Composite level or grade
data_elements.description: Categorical composite result such as a level, grade or severity band.

data_elements.name: Result vector expression
data_elements.description: Compact expression of the inputs that produced the composite score.

artifacts.name: Score report or scorecard
artifacts.description: The rendition of criterion-level and composite results for a reader, carrying the aggregation model identifier, the scale reference and the result vector needed to interpret the numbers.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Series key is the assessment identifier; a zero-padded sequence increments per issued revision. Each revision cites the assessment version and the aggregation model version it was produced under.

findings.name: Conclusion statement, authority and qualification
findings.description: The stated conclusion and its form, the actor accountable for it and whether the decision was separated from the determination work, the qualifications, adverse opinions or dissent attached, and what the conclusion entitles or obliges.

questions.text: What is the stated conclusion, and is it binary, graded or narrative?
answer_data: Scope of the subject the conclusion covers

questions.text: Who is accountable for the conclusion, and was the decision separated from the determination work?
What qualifications, adverse opinions, dissent or minority positions attach to the conclusion?
answer_data: Dissenting or minority position with its author
Conditions attached to a qualified positive conclusion

questions.text: What does the conclusion entitle or oblige, and which downstream act, if any, must follow?
answer_data: Referral to the attestation or certification act
Explicit statement that no legal effect is claimed where none exists

data_elements.name: Conclusion statement
data_elements.description: The stated conclusion of the assessment.

data_elements.name: Conclusion type

data_elements.name: Decision maker reference
data_elements.description: Party accountable for the recorded conclusion.

data_elements.name: Dissent or qualification note
data_elements.description: Recorded qualification, adverse opinion or minority position.

artifacts.name: Assessment report or statement of conclusion
artifacts.description: The authoritative rendition of the conclusion with its scope, criteria binding, decision rule, qualifications and validity, issued to the requesting and relying parties.
artifacts.identity_strategy: The assessing body's master-system report number takes priority; revisions are new zero-padded sequence numbers within the same series, each citing the revision it supersedes. Where no body-issued number exists, a Dimension-assigned UUID bound to the assessment identifier is used.

findings.name: Validity window, conditions and confidence
findings.description: From when until when the conclusion is asserted to hold, the conditions whose breach voids it early, the surveillance or re-assessment needed to keep it current, and the confidence or assurance level claimed.

questions.text: From when until when is the conclusion asserted to hold?
Which conditions, if breached, void the conclusion before its end date?
answer_data: Party obliged to report a breach
Effect of a breach on dependent attestations

questions.text: What ongoing surveillance or re-assessment is required to keep the conclusion current?
answer_data: Consequence of a missed surveillance cycle

questions.text: What confidence or assurance level is claimed, and on what basis?
answer_data: Basis for the claim (depth, coverage, sampling, package)

data_elements.name: Valid from
data_elements.description: Time from which the conclusion is asserted to hold.

data_elements.name: Valid until
data_elements.description: Time at which the conclusion ceases to be asserted.

data_elements.name: Validity condition
data_elements.description: Condition whose breach voids the conclusion early.

data_elements.name: Confidence or assurance level
data_elements.description: Claimed level of confidence or assurance with its basis.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Validity is expressed as timestamps, conditions and a claimed assurance level that consumers must evaluate programmatically before relying on a conclusion. Surveillance activities themselves are executed under the referenced scheme or programme model, and any certificate that carries these dates is issued by the attestation model.

bundles.name: Assurance of the Assessment Itself
bundles.description: Whether the people, tools and instrument behind the result can be relied on.
bundles.rationale: EU law makes legal effect depend on the designation of the body rather than the quality of the method; ILAC and ISO/IEC 17025 make impartiality and competence preconditions of a statement of conformity; and the AERA/APA/NCME Standards make validity, reliability and fairness foundational. Assurance of the assessor and the instrument is therefore a separate concern from the result itself.

layers.name: Assessor and Independence
layers.description: Who performed the assessment, in what roles, with what competence and authorisation, and under what declared conflicts.

findings.name: Assessor identity, roles and contribution
findings.description: Which persons, teams, bodies or automated agents performed the assessment, how the roles of collecting, determining, reviewing and deciding were distributed, and which parts of the result are attributable to which agent.

questions.text: Which persons, teams, bodies or automated agents performed the assessment?
answer_data: Assessor references with their owning party model
Whether each assessor is human, organisational or automated
Team composition where a panel acted

questions.text: How are the roles of collecting, determining, reviewing and deciding distributed?
answer_data: Party acting on behalf of another

questions.text: Which parts of the result are attributable to which assessor or agent?
answer_data: Attribution links from determinations to agents
Activity start and end times per agent
Plan or procedure the agent acted under

data_elements.name: Assessor reference

data_elements.name: Assessor role
data_elements.description: Role in which an assessor acted.

data_elements.name: Attribution link
data_elements.description: Association between a recorded determination and the agent responsible for it.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Assessor identity and role assignment are references into the party model plus PROV-style attribution links. Personnel records, employment status and organisational structure are maintained by that referenced model, so this finding holds pointers and role codes only.

findings.name: Competence, authorisation and impartiality
findings.description: The competence, qualification or accreditation supporting each assessor's participation, the designated scope within which the assessing body may act, declared relationships that could impair impartiality, and what the assessment explicitly does not entitle the assessor to assert.

questions.text: What competence, qualification or accreditation supports each assessor's participation?
answer_data: Accreditation or certification reference with validity

questions.text: Within what designated or accredited scope is the assessing body entitled to act here?
answer_data: Scope of accreditation covering these criteria
Whether the scope covers the subject and criteria assessed

questions.text: What relationships, interests or prior work could impair impartiality, and how were they treated?
What does this assessment explicitly not entitle the assessor to assert?
answer_data: Statement where no legal or regulatory effect arises

data_elements.name: Competence reference
data_elements.description: Pointer to the competence or qualification record supporting participation.

data_elements.name: Accreditation or designation reference
data_elements.description: Pointer to the accreditation, notification or designation held by the assessing body.

data_elements.name: Authorisation scope
data_elements.description: Scope within which the body is entitled to act for these criteria.

data_elements.name: Conflict declaration

findings.inline_only_rationale: Competence, accreditation and designation are asserted and maintained by accreditation authorities and party registries; this finding carries their identifiers, validity and scope plus a locally authored conflict declaration. Reproducing accreditation certificates here would copy content owned by the accreditation registry and risk asserting a status this model cannot verify.

layers.name: Quality Control and Instrument Quality
layers.description: Review and moderation of this assessment, and the standing evidence that the instrument measures what the conclusion claims, reliably and fairly.

findings.name: Review, moderation and rater agreement
findings.description: The independent review, second marking or moderation performed before finalisation, the inter-rater or inter-tool agreement measured against a threshold, and how disagreements between assessors or tools were resolved.

questions.text: What independent review, second marking or moderation was performed before finalisation?
answer_data: Reviewer reference and independence from the determiner
Review outcome and any returned items

questions.text: What inter-rater or inter-tool agreement was measured, and what threshold applied?
answer_data: Sample on which agreement was computed

questions.text: How were disagreements between assessors or tools resolved?
answer_data: Resolution method (adjudication, third rater, precedence rule)

data_elements.name: Review record

data_elements.name: Agreement statistic

data_elements.name: Disagreement resolution method
data_elements.description: Method used to settle conflicting determinations.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Review is a function of this assessment recorded as structured events, statistics and outcomes attached to the record. ISO/IEC 17000 treats review as an internal function preceding the decision rather than a deliverable, and the review's visible output is carried in the assessment report already declared.

findings.name: Instrument validity, reliability and fairness evidence
findings.description: The standing evidence that the instrument measures what the conclusion claims, that its results are precise and repeatable, that bias and accessibility barriers across subject groups have been checked, and the populations or contexts for which it is not validated.

questions.text: What evidence supports that the instrument measures what the conclusion claims?
answer_data: Intended interpretation and use the evidence supports

questions.text: What evidence supports the precision and repeatability of the results?
answer_data: Conditions under which it was estimated
Standard error relevant at the cut score

questions.text: What checks were made for bias, differential functioning or accessibility barriers across subject groups?
answer_data: Subgroups examined and any disparities found

questions.text: For which populations, contexts or subject types is the instrument not validated?
answer_data: Warning required when used outside them

data_elements.name: Reliability statistic

data_elements.name: Fairness check
data_elements.description: Recorded bias, differential-functioning or accessibility check.

data_elements.name: Population or context limit
data_elements.description: Population or context for which the instrument is not validated.

artifacts.name: Instrument validation or technical report
artifacts.description: The standing documentation of validity, reliability and fairness evidence for the instrument, referenced by every assessment that uses it rather than restated per assessment.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Publisher identifier and edition of the instrument documentation where published; a Dimension-assigned UUID plus version for internally developed instruments. Referenced by identifier rather than copied when it is externally published.

bundles.name: Lifecycle, Disclosure and Interoperability
bundles.description: How the record moves through its states, how it is corrected and challenged, who may see what, how long it is kept, and how it projects into external formats.
bundles.rationale: OSCAL requires record identity and last-modified to change on every content change; FHIR supplies an explicit status vocabulary including entered-in-error; the AERA/APA/NCME Standards give test takers rights that imply an appeal route; EU law limits who may publish a result with legal effect; and EARL, XCCDF, OSCAL and QTI all define incompatible result vocabularies that must be crosswalked deliberately.

layers.name: Record Lifecycle
